title: QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence

    Title:QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:High-quality pre-training data is a critical bottleneck for educational and STEM-specific language models targeting edge AI and on-device deployment where token budgets are tightly constrained. While major organizations train ever-larger models on private corpora, the open ecosystem lacks STEM-focused synthetic datasets that deliver high per-token learning value efficiently for small models. To address this gap, we introduce QVAC Genesis III, a 191.43B-token, STEM-focused multi-domain synthetic corpus covering 19 domains across several difficulty levels and different educational styles. QVAC Genesis III is built via a dual generation strategy that performs targeted teacher distillation using a weak edge-scale student model as signal: the student's failures are converted into corrective explanations, while its successes are expanded into contrastive option-level reasoning over all answer choices. We further introduce an LLM-as-a-parser evaluation protocol that extracts final answers from free-form outputs and tracks both accuracy and answer validity. To validate the effectiveness of our QVAC Genesis III data, we conduct controlled from-scratch ablations with 1.7B-parameter models, showing that models trained with QVAC Genesis III consistently outperform both models trained with the open-source synthetic corpus Cosmopedia-v2 and the publicly released Cosmo-1B model across ARC, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU STEM benchmarks, achieving up to +28.57% on ARC-E and +21.35% on ARC-C, while reaching a Valid Answer Rate of up to 99.45%.

report.summary: QVAC Genesis III releases a 191.43B-token open synthetic STEM corpus and shows small models can learn more efficiently for edge AI.
report.background: Pre-training data is a major bottleneck for STEM-focused language models, especially small models meant for edge and on-device use where token budgets are tight. Large labs train on private corpora, leaving the open ecosystem short of high-quality, STEM-specific synthetic datasets that offer strong per-token learning value. Recent work has explored synthetic textbooks, distillation, and benchmark-driven data generation, but much of it targets general web text or very large models. QVAC Genesis III responds to this gap by building a large open corpus aimed at efficient pre-training for compact educational and STEM models, while also proposing a stricter evaluation method for free-form answers.
key_points: QVAC Genesis III provides a 191.43B-token synthetic STEM corpus spanning 19 domains, several difficulty levels, and different educational styles. It is designed to be open and STEM-focused, filling a gap in public pre-training resources for small, education-oriented, and edge-deployable language models that cannot rely on massive token budgets.

The corpus is generated through a dual strategy using a weak edge-scale student model as a signal. Its failures become corrective explanations, while its successes become contrastive option-level reasoning over all answer choices. This targeted teacher distillation turns student mistakes and strengths into training data calibrated to small-model weaknesses.

The paper introduces an LLM-as-a-parser evaluation protocol that extracts final answers from free-form model outputs and tracks both accuracy and answer validity. This matters because generative models often produce correct reasoning but malformed final answers, so validity rate adds a practical reliability dimension beyond standard benchmark accuracy.

Controlled from-scratch ablations with 1.7B-parameter models show QVAC Genesis III outperforms both Cosmopedia-v2-trained models and the public Cosmo-1B across ARC, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU STEM. Gains reach up to +28.57% on ARC-E and +21.35% on ARC-C, with a valid answer rate up to 99.45%.

The work targets efficient pre-training under tight token budgets rather than scaling alone. Its claims suggest specialized synthetic STEM data can deliver higher per-token learning value than general open synthetic corpora, which is especially relevant for on-device educational AI and low-resource model development.
report.impact: For the AI industry, QVAC Genesis III strengthens the case for open, domain-specific synthetic data as an alternative to private mega-corpora and brute-force scale. It could push more labs to release STEM-focused pre-training sets and to evaluate free-form answer validity, not just accuracy. For developers, it offers a potential shortcut to training compact educational or edge models with fewer tokens, though results are limited to 1.7B parameters and specific benchmarks. For regular users, better small STEM models could mean more capable offline tutors, study assistants, and on-device reasoning tools. The main caveats are synthetic-data quality, benchmark overfitting risk, and the need for independent replication beyond STEM tasks.
report.tools: Readers can follow the paper’s data and code release, then compare against Cosmopedia-v2 and Cosmo-1B. Useful follow-up tools include Hugging Face Datasets for loading synthetic corpora, EleutherAI’s lm-evaluation-harness for ARC, MMLU, and GPQA benchmarking, and evaluation frameworks that support LLM-as-a-parser. For on-device deployment, watch llama.cpp and similar edge inference toolkits. Monitor QVAC Genesis III’s Hugging Face repository, arXiv HTML/PDF, and small-model STEM leaderboards for reproducibility updates.
